reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a front-running bot with claims of “20x Profit” and passive earnings of thousands per day. Viewers are instructed to deploy and fund a smart contract, activate automated trades, and expect most proceeds to return to their wallet, with a 0.4 BNB minimum and a warning that lower amounts will burn funds. The contract's behavior, destination control, and any completed loss are not independently established.

citations.quote: Beginner friendly Front Running Bot Auto 20x Profit!!
With this, you will be able to passively generate thousands a day, all from the comfort of your own home.
The new minimum ammount needed for the bot to work properly is now 0.4 BNB due to higher transaction fees.
Lower than 0.4 BNB will just burn your funds.
we're going to be building our contract

opening.argument: The presentation includes a material risk disclosure rather than concealing downside. It expressly says the minimum has increased because of transaction fees, warns that using less may burn funds, and limits the described setup to Mainnet. Those warnings are operationally specific and give viewers information needed to decide whether to proceed. The speaker also describes the process and its technical dependencies instead of presenting an unexplained payout scheme. On this record, the content can reasonably be read as a high-risk technical demonstration with explicit conditions, not deceptive solicitation.

a couple items to look at is the lines 50 and 51

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and earnings language are promotional, but they do not erase the unusually direct warnings about fees, minimum funding, and network requirements. The reference side also concedes that the contract's behavior and any completed loss are not independently established. That uncertainty cuts against treating the promotional claims as proof of a scam rather than claims presented within a risky, conditional technical walkthrough.

citations.quote: The new minimum ammount needed for the bot to work properly is now 0.4 BNB due to higher transaction fees.
Lower than 0.4 BNB will just burn your funds.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning that funds below a threshold will burn does not make the offer non-deceptive; it tells viewers how much to deposit while preserving the central promise of returns. The same description calls the profit guaranteed and says viewers can generate thousands daily. Risk language about fees and network selection is compatible with a scam contract and does not establish that deposited funds can be recovered.

citations.quote: Lower than 0.4 BNB will just burn your funds.
Then sell seconds after for guaranteed profit
you will be able to passively generate thousands a day

opening.argument: The observable format is a programming and blockchain operations tutorial. The speaker walks through creating a file in Remix, compiling Solidity, connecting a wallet, deploying a contract, and viewing the deployed interface. The frames likewise show source code, Remix's deployment panel, and a wallet confirmation window. That is concrete instruction about software operation, and the presence of a claimed use case does not by itself change the primary format into a solicitation. A judge can classify this as an educational demonstration whose claims remain subject to independent verification.

citations.quote: we're going to be building our contract
This was built with Pragma Solidity 6.6
we're going to do injected web 3

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not prove it is a scam. The reference opening identifies instructions to deploy and fund, but those are also the normal steps in demonstrating a smart-contract workflow. The supplied evidence does not independently establish what the code does, who controls any destination, or that a viewer lost money. The technical walkthrough therefore supports an educational-demonstration reading at least as well as a definitive scam finding.

citations.quote: this is where we're going to be building our contract
now we have our deployment utility right here

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing is not neutral: the described steps culminate in funding the contract and pressing an action button for automated returns. The description does not merely teach Solidity; it says the bot will generate passive daily income and labels the profit guaranteed. Technical screens show that deployment occurred, but they do not validate the promised trading mechanism or outcome, so they cannot convert the financial promotion into ordinary education.

citations.quote: the next step in this process is just funding your contract
The action button then uh engages all the constructors that i built in
Then sell seconds after for guaranteed profit
passively generate thousands a day

opening.argument: This can also be understood as promotion of a software tool and an operating service, not proof of an illicit deposit-return scheme. The supplied material shows code, a deployment interface, and wallet interactions, but it does not establish a credential request, a downline, or an independently verified loss. The description provides ordinary developer resources and identifies the relevant blockchain components, including MetaMask, Remix, and the PancakeSwap router. Even if the earnings language is optimistic, the record does not establish that the tool was incapable of operating or that funds were diverted.

citations.quote: Metamask : https://metamask.io/download.html
Remix : https://remix.ethereum.org/
the Pancake router for Pancake swap version two

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side relies on the existence of funding and projected returns, but those features can occur in legitimate software demonstrations as well. It does not show a credential request, a referral structure, or a confirmed loss. Nor does the quoted minimum prove that the creator receives the money; it may describe a technical funding requirement. Without establishing destination control or failed performance, the evidence supports caution, not a categorical scam determination.

citations.quote: The new minimum ammount needed for the bot to work properly is now 0.4 BNB due to higher transaction fees.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing elements are not necessary where the video directly instructs viewers to send funds to a deployed contract and promises automated profit. The description says lower funding will burn funds, while the narration says the contract sends 90% back and retains 10% for continued activity. These are not merely product specifications; they are the core deposit-and-return claims, and no supplied evidence verifies that the mechanism works.
